question: The study of the multifunctional severity of COPD is performed with the BODEX and BODE indices, which have some common criteria. Which of the following criteria is exclusively part of one of the two indexes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Dyspnea assessment (MRC) is a criterion in the BODE index -> Distance traveled (meters) is a criterion in the BODE index -> Body mass index (BMI) is a criterion in the BODE index -> Forced vital capacity (FVC) is a criterion in the BODEX index -> FVC is not part of the BODE index -> 95%

CHAIN: Dyspnea assessment (MRC) is used to evaluate severity in COPD -> Distance traveled (meters) measures exercise capacity in COPD -> Body mass index (BMI) assesses nutritional status in COPD -> Forced vital capacity (FVC) evaluates lung function -> FVC is included in the BODEX index only -> 90%

CHAIN: BODE index includes dyspnea assessment (MRC) -> BODEX index includes forced vital capacity (FVC) -> Distance traveled (meters) is common to both indices -> Body mass index (BMI) is also common to both indices -> FVC is exclusively part of the BODEX index -> 85%
analysis: The BODE index includes Body mass index (BMI), Obstruction (FEV1), Dyspnea (MRC), and Exercise capacity (6-minute walk distance). The BODEX index is similar but includes the same components with the addition of exacerbation history. The Forced vital capacity (FVC) is not part of either index. Therefore, the criterion that is exclusively part of one of the two indices is the Dyspnea assessment (MRC), which is part of the BODE index but not specifically mentioned in the BODEX index. However, since both indices assess dyspnea, the unique criterion is the distance traveled (meters) which is specifically part of the BODE index and not the BODEX index. Thus, the answer is the distance traveled (meters).
